piOfficeNew: A bigger office. I now have more room to walk around a difficult question.
The practice has expanded. I should make sure the standards came with it.
More space. Same detective. The room is taking a cautious interest.
I can finally stand somewhere that is not directly beside my next task.
A proper headquarters. I should avoid expecting the address to solve anything.
The old office kept me close to the work. This one permits a more ceremonial approach.
I have upgraded the premises. My judgement will still need to be checked manually.
The extra space makes every unfinished thought look more deliberately placed.
I should furnish this place for the work I do, not the interview I imagine giving.
The office looks ready for a larger operation. I should begin with one well-handled case.
A bigger business starts with doing the small things properly. Disappointingly familiar advice.
Plenty of room for professional development. I should not fill all of it with objects.

computer: A larger office has not made the inbox more selective.
The computer still handles the adverts. Fortunately, the clients do not need a floor plan.
I should check the case before checking the office shop. There is a relationship between those activities.
Office Expansion. A modest title for acquiring managerial responsibilities.
More applications, same need to read the message before replying.
New premises. The computer continues to expect me to supply the judgement.
phone: The telephone. My business can sound established from exactly one carefully chosen sentence.
A bigger office does not make an awkward question any smaller.
I should check my notes before calling. The room cannot prompt me.
The client hears my voice, not the square footage. Probably for the best.
The receiver still has two useful ends: speaking and listening.
A professional telephone manner is mostly allowing the other person to finish lying.
cityDoor: The office is worth coming back to. I should now give myself a reason to leave.
New headquarters, same city. Best not expect anyone outside to applaud.
An impressive office is not an alibi for avoiding fieldwork.
I should take the relevant notes. The rest of the business can remain indoors.
The city has not become less complicated while I was improving the office.
Time to investigate something that cannot be rearranged on a floor plan.
books: Books. Useful references, provided I occasionally consult the parts behind the spines.
A respectable collection. I should resist quoting something I have only read on the cover.
The answer might be in a book. The question is still my responsibility.
Reference material. A more reliable source than vaguely remembering a conversation.
painting: A painting. It gives visitors something to study while deciding how much to tell me.
An office can have taste without claiming expertise in attribution.
I bought something to look at. An unusually honest purpose for office decor.
I should not start deducing the artist from the frame. I have actual work.
artifact: A display piece. I should keep its decorative role separate from my professional curiosity.
Interesting object. "Interesting" is not a verified provenance.
The office now contains a conversation piece. I still have to supply the conversation.
I should not let an impressive display do the work of an actual explanation.
chairs: Visitor chairs. A practical investment in hearing the entire story.
Providing a seat is not the same as providing reassurance. It is a reasonable opening.
The clients can sit down. Their version of events may still need support.
Chairs make an interview more comfortable. The questions can handle the opposite.
coffee: Coffee. A courtesy, not an interrogation technique.
I should let the client finish speaking before offering a second explanation and a second coffee.
An office with coffee. My professional credentials remain under separate review.
Coffee improves a meeting. It does not validate the conclusions.
tv: A television. The city can now bring its problems into my office electronically.
Local news. Useful context, provided I distinguish reporting from dramatic music.
An authoritative voice is not the same as a reliable source. Even with a studio.
I should not mistake being informed for having investigated.
crimeBoard: A board for my investigations. Each connection still has to earn its place.
More space for evidence. Not an invitation to collect unrelated suspicions.
The client wants an answer. The board should show why that answer deserves to be believed.
A visual theory. Best check that removing the lines would not remove the entire argument.
caseFiles: Completed cases belong in the records, not in my increasingly heroic recollection.
A case file should explain what happened without requiring me to stand beside it.
An archive of my own work. A useful defence against confidently forgetting it.
Filed properly, a closed case can still answer a new question.
printer: A printer. For when an electronic document needs the additional vulnerability of paper.
The documents need checking before printing. Ink is not a form of verification.
A hard copy. Useful when explaining that I really did read the original.
I should select the right document. The machine is not responsible for my dramatic timing.
notepad: Notes in my own words. I should make a small concession to my future ability to read them.
A useful place for questions. A dangerous place to disguise guesses as facts.
I need dates, names, and exact wording. "Odd fellow" can be a footnote.
Writing it down prevents forgetting. It does not prevent writing down something foolish.

moveInCompleted: Moved in. I should establish where the work happens before deciding where to look successful.
The new office is real now. Any remaining improvements will require decisions rather than optimism.
New premises. I should update my habits before they settle in exactly as they were.
I have more space. The first challenge is remembering why I crossed it.
The move is complete. Back to the business that was supposed to justify it.
itemPurchased: Another office improvement. I should let it become useful before ordering its companion.
Purchase complete. The next stage is using the thing.
I have added to the office. I should now add something to the investigation.
A practical upgrade, I hope. The receipt is making no promises.
noCase: A bigger office and no active job. The classifieds have become particularly relevant.
No current assignment. I should seek work before redesigning the workspace again.
The premises are ready. I need a client problem, not another furniture decision.
I should check the adverts. A business cannot live entirely on looking available.
caseAccepted: New case accepted. This office is about to acquire a purpose for the afternoon.
A client request. Best identify the actual problem before involving the entire room.
Time to put the improved workspace to work. Starting with reading the brief.
I have promised to investigate. The size of the office has not enlarged that promise.
caseCompleted: Another case completed. Good to know the business is more than its furnishings.
Job finished. I should organise the record before the next enquiry arrives.
That case is complete. I shall enjoy the result without improving the story.
A finished investigation. The office now has something useful to be proud of.
expansionStaffHired: A new colleague. I should provide clear instructions rather than mysterious detective gestures.
Hiring complete. "I usually just work it out" is no longer an adequate operating procedure.
The business now includes somebody else. I should stop calling every mistake a personal system.
I have hired a professional. Best allow them to demonstrate what that means.
expansionRentDue: The annex rent is due. The Alibi Fund needs attention before the affected rooms can resume work.
Overdue annex rent. I should check the fund, not my private spending money.
The affected rooms are paused. A clear financial explanation is more useful than blaming morale.
I should review the annex rent in Office Expansion. Floor space has recurring opinions about payment.
